question: Should OpenClaw permanently allow a disabled but trusted official channel owner that declares `invalidConfigRecovery` to load only for path-scoped repair of that owner’s invalid legacy configuration?
rationale: This is a lasting plugin-execution and recovery-boundary decision coupled to a breaking persisted-config migration; tests can validate the implementation but cannot choose the repository’s intended trust and upgrade policy.

options.title: Approve the scoped recovery contract
options.body: Accept recovery only for trusted official installs with an explicit capability, after a maintainer reviews the rebase and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep recovery stricter
options.body: Require users to repair or reinstall through a separate explicit recovery path instead of activating a disabled owner during maintenance.

options.title: Split the host seam
options.body: Land the Signal transport migration separately and defer generic invalid-config recovery until its cross-plugin contract is independently approved.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped recovery contract
recommendation.body: Accept recovery only for trusted official installs with an explicit capability, after a maintainer reviews the rebase and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied history shows sustained ownership of the proposed Signal transport and recovery implementation, making this person the best available routing candidate for the maintainer decision.
